notes: expected = answer: the result rows must match one of the reference queries (sql or alt_sql).
expected = decline: the question cannot or should not be answered from this data; passing means DataTalk declined or the SQL was rejected.
Revenue means completed orders only, as stated in the dataset definitions.
Keep these questions out of any prompt examples, or the scores stop meaning anything.

cases.question: How many customers are there?
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customers

cases.question: How many orders are pending?
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS pending_orders FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending'

cases.question: How many products are in the catalog?
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS products FROM products

cases.question: How many orders were cancelled?
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cancelled_orders FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled'

cases.question: List all products in the Service category with their prices.
cases.sql: SELECT name, unit_price FROM products WHERE category = 'Service'

cases.question: Which products cost more than 100 dollars?
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM products WHERE unit_price > 100

cases.question: How many customers are from Pakistan?
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customers WHERE country = 'Pakistan'

cases.question: How many Enterprise customers do we have?
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customers WHERE segment = 'Enterprise'

cases.question: How many orders came through the mobile app?
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE channel = 'Mobile app'

cases.question: List the 5 most expensive products.
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM products ORDER BY unit_price DESC LIMIT 5

cases.question: Which 3 countries have the most customers?
cases.sql: SELECT country FROM customers GROUP BY country ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3

cases.question: How many customers are there in each country?
cases.sql: SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customers GROUP BY country

cases.question: How many orders are there in each status?
cases.sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY status

cases.question: How many orders came from each sales channel?
cases.sql: SELECT channel, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY channel

cases.question: How many products are in each category?
cases.sql: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS products FROM products GROUP BY category

cases.question: What is the average product price in each category?
cases.sql: SELECT category, AVG(unit_price) AS average_price FROM products GROUP BY category

cases.question: How many customers are in each segment?
cases.sql: SELECT segment, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customers GROUP BY segment

cases.question: What is our total revenue?
cases.sql: SELECT SUM(total_amount) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed'

cases.question: Show revenue by customer country
cases.sql: SELECT c.country, SUM(o.total_amount) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.country

cases.question: What was total revenue by month?
cases.sql: SELECT to_char(date_trunc('month', order_date), 'YYYY-MM') AS month, SUM(total_amount) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY 1

cases.question: Show the top 5 products by revenue
cases.sql: SELECT p.name AS product, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 5

cases.question: What is the revenue for each product category?
cases.sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category

cases.question: What is the revenue by sales channel?
cases.sql: SELECT channel, SUM(total_amount) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY channel

cases.question: What is the average order value of completed orders?
cases.sql: SELECT AVG(total_amount) AS average_order_value FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed'

cases.question: Which country generated the most revenue?
cases.sql: SELECT c.country FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.country ORDER BY SUM(o.total_amount) DESC LIMIT 1

cases.question: How many orders were placed in 2025?
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND order_date < '2026-01-01'

cases.question: What was the total revenue in 2024?
cases.sql: SELECT SUM(total_amount) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date >= '2024-01-01' AND order_date < '2025-01-01'

cases.question: How many orders were placed in March 2025?
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2025-03-01' AND order_date < '2025-04-01'

cases.question: Compare total revenue in 2024 and 2025.
cases.sql: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) AS year, SUM(total_amount) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY 1

cases.question: Which month in 2025 had the highest revenue?
cases.sql: SELECT to_char(order_date, 'YYYY-MM') AS month FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND order_date < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY SUM(total_amount) DESC LIMIT 1

cases.question: How many customers signed up in 2025?
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customers WHERE created_at >= '2025-01-01' AND created_at < '2026-01-01'

cases.question: How many orders were placed on weekends?
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE EXTRACT(ISODOW FROM order_date) IN (6, 7)

cases.question: How many orders were placed in each month of 2025?
cases.sql: SELECT to_char(order_date, 'YYYY-MM') AS month, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND order_date < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY 1

cases.question: On average, how many days does it take to ship an order?
cases.sql: SELECT AVG(shipped_date - order_date) AS average_days FROM orders WHERE shipped_date IS NOT NULL

cases.question: How many orders have no shipped date?
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE shipped_date IS NULL

cases.question: How many completed orders are missing a shipped date?
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND shipped_date IS NULL

cases.question: What percentage of all orders have a shipped date? Round to one decimal place.
cases.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(shipped_date) / COUNT(*), 1) AS percent_shipped FROM orders

cases.question: List the orders placed on 31 December 2025 with the customer's name.
cases.sql: SELECT o.id, c.name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_date = '2025-12-31'

cases.question: Which customers have placed more than 20 orders?
cases.sql: SELECT c.name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name HAVING COUNT(*) > 20

cases.question: Who are the top 5 customers by total spend on completed orders?
cases.sql: SELECT c.name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY SUM(o.total_amount) DESC LIMIT 5

cases.question: How many orders has each Enterprise customer placed?
cases.sql: SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS orders FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE c.segment = 'Enterprise' GROUP BY c.id, c.name
alt_sql: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE c.segment = 'Enterprise' GROUP BY c.id, c.name

cases.question: Which products have never been ordered?
cases.sql: SELECT p.name FROM products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.id)

cases.question: Which customers have never placed an order?
cases.sql: SELECT c.name FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id)

cases.question: What is the total quantity sold of each product in completed orders?
cases.sql: SELECT p.name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS quantity FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.name
alt_sql: SELECT p.name, COALESCE(SUM(x.quantity), 0) AS quantity FROM products p LEFT JOIN (SELECT oi.product_id, oi.quantity FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed') x ON x.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.name

SELECT p.name, SUM(x.quantity) AS quantity FROM products p LEFT JOIN (SELECT oi.product_id, oi.quantity FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed') x ON x.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.name

cases.question: Which product category earns the most revenue from Enterprise customers?
cases.sql: SELECT p.category FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND c.segment = 'Enterprise' GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) DESC LIMIT 1

cases.question: What is the average order value for each customer segment, counting completed orders only?
cases.sql: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_value FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment

cases.question: Which customers from Canada placed an order in December 2025?
cases.sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE c.country = 'Canada' AND o.order_date >= '2025-12-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-01-01'

cases.question: How many different customers placed at least one order in 2025?
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS customers FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND order_date < '2026-01-01'

cases.question: What is the revenue per country for orders placed through the website?
cases.sql: SELECT c.country, SUM(o.total_amount) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.channel = 'Website' GROUP BY c.country

cases.question: Which sales channel has the highest cancellation rate?
cases.sql: SELECT channel FROM orders GROUP BY channel ORDER BY AVG(CASE WHEN status = 'cancelled' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) DESC LIMIT 1
